name: Total Trace Count
definition: For a finite binary class $\mathcal H$ on a finite domain $X$, its **Total Trace Count** is $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal H):=\sum_{S\subseteq X}|\mathcal H_{|S}|$, the number of distinct labeled traces counted over all coordinate subsets.
description: Equivalently, count each pair $(S,h|_S)$ consisting of a coordinate subset and a distinct trace realized on it. This aggregate is finite only for finite domains.
graph_summary: Total number of distinct traces over all coordinate subsets: $\sum_{S\subseteq X}|\mathcal H_{|S}|$.

monotonic.proof: For every coordinate set $S$, a subfamily has a subset of the traces of the ambient class on $S$. Summing over $S$ proves monotonicity.

p_monotonic.proof: For a projection to $T\subseteq X$, the traces of $\mathcal H_{|T}$ are exactly the traces of $\mathcal H$ on coordinate subsets $S\subseteq T$. Their sum is at most the sum over all $S\subseteq X$.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioned fibre is first a subfamily and then a coordinate projection. Apply the two preceding monotonicity arguments.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The direct subfamily and projection arguments establish both parts of doubly monotonicity.
